newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Tesco yr profits may be booster.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Tesco yr profits may be booster.

text.p: Britain's top supermarket group Tesco Plc is expected to show a healthy rise in annual profits when it reports on April 8 and analysts are hoping it will give encouraging signs for the rest of the sector.
"What they say about current conditions could be the key to the sector outperforming," said one sector analyst who declined to be named.
Tesco is forecast to have pretax profits of between 745 and 755 million stg, up from 675 million stg previously and pay out a total dividend of around 10.5 pence, compared with 9.8 pence a year ago.
Tesco's expected rise in results will be welcomed in a sector where two of the other large supermarkets, J. Sainsbury Plc and Safeway Plc, have warned that profits could be below expectations.

Sainsbury, which was bumped off the top slot by Tesco over a year ago, said in January that profits were likely to be around 640-650 million stg, some 50 million stg below forecasts, as the cost of improving sales hurt.
Two weeks later Safeway said slowing sales growth and low inflation could hit profits.
"Encouraging noises are needed on margins and sales growth," the sector analyst said.
Tesco said in January that sales were up 7.5 percent over the key Christmas trading period, outperforming much of the market, and cited "investing in low prices" for the gains.
"Tesco's sales are likely to be at the top end and if they have maintained momentum, that could boost the rest of the sector," the analyst said.
The company, which paid out 630 million stg for the Irish supermarkets of Associated British Foods in March, appears to be moving from strength to strength, analysts said.
"Tesco is clearly on a roll, I don't see any fly in the ointment," the analyst said.
The company might announce further marketing or financial initiatives, analysts said, but no major developments are expected.
Tesco is part of the swelling ranks of supermarkets moving into financial services and has said that it wants to launch a credit card over the summer through its link-up with Royal Bank of Scotland.
"Tesco's at the top of the league, it is doing all the right things and we are expecting a good set of figures," the analyst said. -- London Newsroom +44171 542 7717
